observations.title: emart24 self-checkout
observations.place: Daejeon, emart24 Chungnam National University branch
observations.scenario: Scanning and paying for purchases without a cashier in a convenience store.

unverified: Which payment methods work with a foreign card

media.caption: Self-checkout screen with the printed step guide above it.

observed: A printed guide above the screen shows five steps: prepare, scan barcode, discount or points, pay (card or SSG PAY), done.
The guide adds two rules: scan every item in a 1+1 or 2+1 promotion, and ask staff to process alcohol and tobacco.
The screen repeats the same steps as tabs: 상품등록 (add items), 할인적립 (discounts and points), 결제수단 (payment method), 결제완료 (done).
Each item shows its own discount on a separate red line. Two jellies show −2,000 ₩, so the second one is free (1+1).
Totals: 8,300 ₩, discount −2,600 ₩, to pay 5,700 ₩.
Quick buttons at the bottom cover items without a barcode: shopping bags at 100 and 250 ₩, bottled water.
A 글자확대 (enlarge text) button sits in the bottom bar.
Separate buttons for partner discounts or points and for emart24's own quick payment.
An Apple Pay sticker on the frame. A handwritten yellow sticky note reads 가져가세요 (“please take it”).
interpretation: Discounts and loyalty points are a separate step placed between scanning and payment.
open: How common are 1+1 and 2+1 promotions in Korean convenience stores, and why? Needs a source.
When did Apple Pay launch in Korea? Check.
What does the 가져가세요 note refer to?

observations.title: Hanjin delivery notifications
observations.scenario: Receiving a parcel while not at home.

unverified: Can the drop-off and tracking page be used without a Korean phone number?

media.caption: Step 1. Text message: the courier is on the way.
Step 2. Text message: delivered, with a photo of the drop-off spot.

observed: Both messages come from an ordinary mobile number (+82 10-…), not a short service number.
The first message lists the item name, tracking number, sender, address and a delivery window of 14:00–16:00.
It links to a page for choosing a drop-off spot (위탁장소) and tracking the courier in real time.
It ends by asking the recipient to remove the label and packaging and sort them for recycling.
The second message says the parcel was left at the drop-off spot (문앞, “in front of the door”) because nobody was home, with the exact time 13:39:27.
A photo is attached. It shows a pile of many residents' parcels on the floor of a shared hallway, not a door.
interpretation: The photo works as proof of delivery.
In a dormitory, “in front of the door” in practice means a shared hallway.
open: Is the sender number the courier's personal phone or a masked relay number? Check.
Is the delivery photo a Hanjin standard or up to the courier?
observations.rights: Own screenshots. Phone number, tracking number, address, sender and parcel labels are blurred.

observations.title: SSG.com product page
observations.scenario: Checking a product and its promotions before buying.

unverified: Does buying require identity verification with a Korean phone number (본인인증)?

media.caption: Product page, promotion section and fixed bottom bar.

observed: The product description is made of images with the text set inside them, including promotions (“Benefit 2: free GO5 speaker”) and fine print.
Tabs at the top: 정보 (info), 리뷰 14 (reviews), Q&A 3.
A banner states the seller is an official Samsung online partner selling genuine products.
A fixed bottom bar shows 오늘출발 (“ships today”) for orders paid by 15:00, a gift-box icon button and a large 구매하기 (buy) button.
interpretation: The gift-box icon next to the buy button probably means “send as a gift” (선물하기).
open: Does the icon open a gifting flow? Check by tapping it.
Are image-based product descriptions (상세페이지) standard across Korean online shops? Needs a source. How do screen readers and search handle them?

observations.title: University dormitory app-activated commercial washer
observations.subject: metaclub
observations.scenario: A student activates and pays for a dormitory laundromat washing machine by scanning a machine-mounted QR code using a campus lifestyle mobile app.

requires: Smartphone with camera and internet connection
unverified: Does point charging require a Korean domestic payment method?
Is mobile identity verification (본인인증) strictly required to use laundry functions?

media.caption: In-app promotional popup offering laundry credit rewards
Multilingual QR code sticker mounted on washing machine #6
Front control panel showing courses, duration, and pricing
Top and front panel of washer with usage guidelines
QR code scanner screen within the MetaClub mobile app
MetaClub app home view displaying an ad tracking permission prompt
Popup prompting real-name mobile identity verification
Campus/public contest listing inside the MetaClub app

observed: Washing machine #6 is an LG Commercial Washer with a dedicated sticker containing a QR code labeled 'WA001701'.
The QR sticker includes instructions in Korean, English, Chinese, and Vietnamese directing users to scan with the MetaClub app.
The washing machine control panel displays courses (강력세탁, 표준세탁, 합성세탁, 울세탁, 헹굼추가) and lists 1,200 KRW for standard wash and 300 KRW for extra rinse.
The MetaClub app has an in-app QR scanner prompting 'Scan the QR code on your machine.'
The MetaClub app includes navigation tabs for Laundry, Exchange, Benefit, Teample, and Ticket.
A modal dialog in the app requests ad tracking permission ('광고 추적 허용이 필요합니다') to earn rewards.
Another popup prompts for carrier-based identity verification ('본인 명의 휴대폰이 있다면, 본인인증 후 더 많은 기능과 한도를 이용해 보세요').
interpretation: The commercial washers are networked via Wi-Fi and triggered digitally after QR code recognition in the app rather than accepting physical coins.
The app serves broader campus and lifestyle functions beyond dormitory laundry, such as student contest recruitment and theater ticket sales.
open: Can foreign students without Korean carrier identity verification register and use the laundry feature without limitations?
Does the machine start automatically once payment is finalized in the app, or does the user still need to push the physical START button?
observations.rights: Own material. Personal data blurred automatically; reviewed before publication.
